scope: Ordinary authored foot-route door assistance, not a new assault controller or whole LAMBS parity.

references.readScope: Complete helper; original source kept read-only

sourceIntent: LAMBS responds through individual native-task/unit actions. Its CQB helper also redirects movement and consumes building positions probabilistically; those semantics are not adopted here. This comparison exposed the separate CBE group-level selection bottleneck.
finding: CBE ended route-door observation after its first eligible actor even with no house ahead. Later moving actors with a real door waited for later group callbacks.
implementation: Try at most4 eligible approaches inside the existing rotating16-actor/64-member window and2s minimum callback gap.
Empty/irrelevant approaches continue; stop after one actual opening request. Cursor advances after each attempted actor, including failed approaches.

Reuse the local sampled native goal; actual animation helper still rechecks ownership/epoch/plain MOVE/locks/near visibility/narrow approach. No new route, movement worker, distant opening, room visit or clearance credit.
cost: Up to4 short3m approach rays plus16 nearby door visibility rays, replacing prior1+4 bound. No added radius query or recurring worker. Average/worst frame impact and real response timing require measurement.
remaining: Physical native routing through terrain/editor/Zeus buildings, repeated door use and frame-time cost remain unverified; audits paused.
Full CQB handover and tactical flow remain incomplete.
